title.title: The Correspondence of the Yarnall family

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of the Yarnall family is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: I may inform thee that I have received a few lines from thee dated the 8th of the 12 mo, which was satisfactory to we to hear thee was pretty well in health. Though very sorry for thy toothache, which I know to be a very afflicting disorder. The time will seem very long to me if thee lets it be till spring before thee comes to see me, but if it is right, I hope I shall submit if thee don’t come. Please do write & let me know how you all are, & if sister is likely to have the use of her arm. I may inform thee that I have been very poorly taken at the preparative meeting, but now am some considerable better. The rest of the family pretty well, except John some poorly with a cold. I may inform thee that I wrote to thee since I sent the last sender. By what thee wrote was fearful thee did not receive it.

closer.salute: So I conclude and remain thy loving & affectionate Mother,

postscript.p: Please to remember me & my husband to Brother & Sister & little James & Jamie & all the rest of my best friends
